pages.text: All around, waves sparkle and move. In the middle sits Ivy, a piece of land wrapped in water.
Water touches Ivy on every side. That is what makes Ivy an island.
Some islands are tiny dots. Others are big enough to have cities, roads, and farms.
Soft beaches stretch along Ivy’s edges. Sand meets water again and again.
Inside the island, trees and plants grow. Some islands even have hills or mountains.
Boats arrive carrying people and supplies. Water connects islands to the rest of the world.
Animals live here too. Birds fly over the water, and fish swim nearby.
Some islands were made by volcanoes. Others broke away from bigger land long ago.
Ivy reminds us: water shapes island life, travel, and weather every day.
At bedtime, we remember: islands are land surrounded by water, full of life and stories.
